clue.text: A boy in a rush, that's clear

indicators.note: in places the letters for 'A boy' inside the word for the plant

parts.note: a rush is a waterside plant, also called a reed
a boy is someone's son

explanation.surface: A lad dashing about somehow manages to be lucid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rush' looks like haste, but it is the waterside plant, and 'clear' is an adjective meaning lucid.
explanation.definitionFit: A reasoned argument is logical and lucid, so it is clear.

clue.text: Was bombastic before in a way

indicators.note: in places the word for before inside the abbreviation for a road

parts.note: RD is the abbreviation for road, a way
ante is Latin for before, as in ante-room

explanation.surface: A speaker was pompous earlier in some manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a way' looks like a hedging phrase, but 'way' is the road abbreviation that holds the Latin word.
explanation.definitionFit: To rant is to speak in a loud, pompous, inflated way, which is bombast.

clue.text: Girl giving a Pole a leg up

parts.note: N stands for the North Pole

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the words a leg are read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A young woman helps a Polish man climb up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a Polish person, but it is N for north; 'up' turns A LEG into GELA.
explanation.definitionFit: Angela is a woman's first name, so an example of a girl.

clue.text: Not at home with the Tories entirely

parts.note: someone not at home is out
the Tories, Britain's Conservative Party, are the political right

explanation.surface: Someone sided with the Conservatives wholly while away from home.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tories are Britain's Conservative Party, on the political right.
explanation.definitionFit: Outright means completely or wholly, a synonym for entirely.

clue.text: Some quiet once-famous place on the Thames

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A sleepy riverside town that used to be well known.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton, home of the famous school, lies on the Thames opposite Windsor.
explanation.definitionFit: Eton is a town on the river opposite Windsor, known for its public school.

parts.note: a swell is a rounded protrusion, a bulge

explanation.surface: Someone points out an extra swelling as well as the first.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as A SWELL, a bulge; read whole it means 'in addition'.
explanation.definitionFit: As well means also, in addition, a synonym for too.

indicators.note: the second as is read as 'when turned into', so the words As mean are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone claims mariners are notoriously stingy.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter gives no clearer signal than the second 'as': AS MEAN rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A seaman is a mariner, someone who works at sea.

indicators.note: in places the word of approval inside the rowing crew

parts.note: an eight is a rowing crew of eight oarsmen
yes is a word of agreement or approval

explanation.surface: Someone detects agreement among the team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crew' suggests sailors, but it is a rowing EIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyesight is the faculty of seeing, one of the five senses.

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty, a crossword stand-in for many
earners are people who work for a wage

explanation.surface: Lots of employees are apprentices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Many' gives L, the Roman fifty.
explanation.definitionFit: Learners are people being taught, synonyms for trainees.

indicators.note: a new presentation or staging of the play's name reworks its letters into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A ban is placed on staging the Greek tragedy Antigone.
explanation.walkthrough: Antigone is a Greek tragedy by Sophocles; its eight letters rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A veto is a refusal or denial, a synonym for negation.

clue.text: Georgia and Lena together giving lead

parts.note: GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia
the name taken as written

explanation.surface: Two women team up to give a lead to others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' looks like guidance, but it is the metal: galena is its chief ore.
explanation.definitionFit: Galena is lead sulphide, the main mineral from which the metal is extracted.

indicators.note: blunders, read as a verb, says the word Reveals stumbles into a new order

explanation.surface: An inquiry exposes a fair number of mistakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blunders' looks like a plural noun, but it is a verb signalling a rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Several means more than two but not many, a modest number.

parts.note: EC is the postcode district of the City of London, its financial heart
a lair is a den or hideaway, a retreat

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a cake to take away from the town as a refuge.
explanation.definitionFit: An eclair is a long choux pastry filled with cream, a kind of small cake.

indicators.note: odd suggests the word Oriental is put into a strange new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone remarks on a curious link with the East.
explanation.definitionFit: A relation is a link or association between things, a connection.

parts.note: a bird readies itself for flight by tidying its feathers with its beak

explanation.surface: Someone got ready to take off.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a traveller; the picture is of a bird grooming its plumage.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds groom their feathers before flying, and to groom so is to preen.

clue.text: Person using a credit card to get a dish

explanation.surface: A shopper pays by plastic to buy a plate.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who charges a purchase pays on credit; a charger is also a large flat serving plate.

explanation.surface: Someone tells the cook to blacken the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: To char is to scorch; a char is also a trout-like fish of cold lakes.

clue.text: Give voice about a pest getting attached

indicators.note: about means the word for give voice goes around the word for the pest

parts.note: to give voice is to sing
a tick is a blood-sucking parasite, a pest

explanation.surface: Someone shouts about a nuisance that clings on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Give voice' looks like complaining, and 'pest' like any nuisance; the pest is the parasitic bug.
explanation.definitionFit: Sticking means adhering, so becoming fixed or attached.

clue.text: Impressed on egghead the need for dash

parts.note: to impress is to stamp a mark on something
read as egg-head: the head or first letter of egg

explanation.surface: Someone told a clever person they needed to hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Egghead' looks like an intellectual, but split it: the head of 'egg' is E, placed on (after) STAMPED.
explanation.definitionFit: A stampede is a sudden mass rush, so a dash.

clue.text: Homily about the short answer-to prosecute

indicators.note: about means the word for homily goes around the short answer

parts.note: a tract is a short religious treatise, a homily
ANS is a common abbreviation for answer

explanation.surface: A sermon on a brief reply leads someone to take legal action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prosecute' suggests a court, but here it means carry out, as to prosecute a war.
explanation.definitionFit: To prosecute in the older sense is to pursue or carry through, which is to transact.

clue.text: Picture gallery in a stately home

indicators.note: in tells us the gallery's name sits inside the letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Paintings are displayed in a grand country house.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate is a group of London art galleries; the letters sit inside 'stately'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tate is a famous national art gallery in London, so a picture gallery by name.

indicators.note: hold means the word for salesmen goes around the word for music

parts.note: reps is short for sales representatives
an air is a tune, a piece of music

explanation.surface: Sales staff put customers on hold with music, which is supposed to soothe them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hold music' looks like a phone waiting tune, but 'hold' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Repairs are mendings, and mending is a kind of restoration akin to healing.

parts.note: pop is an informal word for father
in means inside

explanation.surface: Dad left the material indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stuff' looks like a verb, but it is a noun meaning fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Stuff is an old word for woven fabric, and poplin is a ribbed cotton cloth.

indicators.note: vandalising wrecks the word amused, so its letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Wrecking things gave the ogre a laugh.
explanation.walkthrough: Medusa is the snake-haired Gorgon of Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: Medusa is the Gorgon whose gaze turned onlookers to stone, a mythical monster.

clue.text: National transport is to take it over

parts.note: BR stands for British Rail, the former national railway
taken as written
on means over or on top of

explanation.surface: A country's railway is meant to absorb the extra traffic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'National' looks like an adjective but is a noun, a citizen; BR was British Rail.
explanation.definitionFit: A Briton is a citizen of the UK, and a national is a citizen of a country.

parts.note: note-paper here means paper ruled with musical staves, where a composer first writes a piece

explanation.surface: Someone first drafted a letter on writing paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note-paper' suggests letters, but the notes are musical.
explanation.definitionFit: Music that is composed is created by its author, often first set down on manuscript paper.

parts.note: to finish is to end
the ear is the body's equipment for hearing sound

explanation.surface: A hi-fi buyer completes a purchase of audio gear and wins a prize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound equipment' suggests speakers, but it is the human ear.
explanation.definitionFit: To endear is to win affection, as in winning someone over.

clue.text: A staff of a thousand and one

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
an ace is the one in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: Someone describes an office team of a thousand and one people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' suggests employees, but it is a ceremonial rod.
explanation.definitionFit: A mace is a ceremonial rod carried as a symbol of authority, a kind of staff.

indicators.note: to fashion is to shape, so the letters of the women's word are reshaped

explanation.surface: Women's clothing has its own standards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fashion' looks like clothing, but it is a verb signalling a rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideals are standards of perfection by which things are judged, so criteria.

clue.text: Shy on release after doing a stretch

definitions.text: Shy on release after doing a stretch

parts.words: Shy on release after doing a stretch
parts.note: the device is pulled back and let go to hurl a stone; to shy is to throw

explanation.surface: A timid convict, freed after a prison sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shy' looks like timid and 'doing a stretch' like serving time; in fact a stretched elastic flings an object.
explanation.definitionFit: A catapult is a forked stick with elastic that throws stones when the stretched band is released.

parts.note: green means naive or inexperienced

explanation.surface: An author of simple English prose.
explanation.walkthrough: Graham Greene was an English novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: Graham Greene, author of Brighton Rock, was a celebrated novelist.

indicators.note: to exercise is to work out, so the word trainers is worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone keeps a firm grip on the people who run fitness sessions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trainers exercise' reads as coaches working out; 'exercise' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To restrain is to hold back or keep in check, a synonym for control.
